questions.q: What is flow, according to the passage?
options: A state of full absorption where skill and challenge are balanced
A form of meditation aimed at deep relaxation and reduced arousal
A medical condition of attention found in autism and ADHD patients
A technique for working faster under pressure by raising stress levels
questions.explain: Flow is a mental state of energized focus and full involvement, balancing skill and challenge.

options: It was named after a mountain stream
People used a water-current metaphor to describe how it felt
It described the flow of information in the brain
The founder was a swimmer
questions.explain: Interviewees said things like 'I was carried on by the flow' as though by a water current.

questions.q: About how much information per second can the mind attend to, per Csikszentmihalyi's TED talk?
options: About 11 bits
About 40 bits
About 110 bits
About 1,100 bits
questions.explain: The number given is about 110 bits per second, with decoding speech using 40-60 bits.

questions.q: What can the flow questionnaire NOT measure?
options: Whether people have experienced flow
Differences in likelihood across factors
The prevalence of flow
The intensity of flow during specific activities
questions.explain: The FQ does not allow measurement of intensity of flow during specific activities.

questions.q: Which example would the passage count as hyperfocus rather than flow?
options: A chess player in balance with the challenge, energized throughout the whole game
Becoming so absorbed in one part of an assignment that the whole assignment suffers
A runner whose pace matches her ability, enjoying the challenge of the race
A student enjoying an exam whose difficulty is well suited to her skills
questions.explain: Hyperfocus is not always positive, such as absorption in one aspect of a task to the detriment of the overall assignment.
